Variable Bit Rate Color Compression with Macro Blocks is a compression format for sparse 3D color data that uses variable bits per weight (bpw) to optimize compression ratio, addressing the limitation of fixed bpw methods where theoretical optimal compression is constrained by header overhead [S1, unofficial].

The claim accurately reflects the content of Source [S1]. The source explicitly describes a compression format for sparse 3D color data that uses variable bits per weight (bpw) to optimize compression ratio. It addresses the limitation of fixed bpw methods (where theoretical optimal compression is constrained by header overhead) by segregating data into macro blocks (specifically 2^14 colors) and using a tree structure to find the optimal bit rate. The source details the header structure (14 bits for index, 16 for bit pointer, 2 for bpw) and the mechanism for handling the fifth case (sentinel). All specific facts mentioned in the claim are present in the provided text.
